type: u32[8] header + u32[count-8] section-relative offsets + 0x1C-byte block
structure: Section-1 header table: registration list of the refcounted record family, root of the loader traversal
meaning: Header words: {0, 0, 0, count, count, 0x80000000|count*4, 0x1C, count*4+0x1C}; count (0xB32 = 2 866 in the tutorial) counts u32 words from the section start including the 8 header words, so the offsets array holds count-8 entries (2 858) and the flagged word is the table end; the block of 7 words that follows holds 6 more section-relative roots (two 0x40-byte type-52 nodes and four RHSValueStack objects at the end of the section) plus 0x800001A7. Every entry is a section-relative offset of a record whose header is {type, refcount 1..6, 0x01xxxxxx}; the family is types 52, 54, 58, 83, 90, 92, 104, 151, 160 (all instances of 52 and 92, e.g. the spawn owner at entry #1074), 68, 88, 151. There are no null (0xFFFFFFFF) slots: the 35 nulls reported earlier were words inside objects, because the array had been placed after its end pointer. At runtime the header becomes an object (class 0x80493758 at +4, count words zeroed, +0x1C -> first object) and every entry becomes a pointer; a heap array copies {first object, entries...}. Growing the table by one entry is possible with the fixup map (igz clone-entity).
